question:
A child of height $1.5\ \text{m}$ walks directly away from a vertical lamp post of height $6\ \text{m}$ at a rate of $1.2\ \text{m/s}$. Let $x$ be the distance of the child from the lamp post and $y$ be the length of the child's shadow.

(a) Using similar triangles, establish a relation between $x$ and $y$.

(b) Determine the rate at which the length of the shadow is increasing.

(c) Find the rate at which the tip of the shadow is moving away from the lamp post.
explanation:
(a)
The distance of the tip of the shadow from the lamp post is $x+y$. By similarity of the triangles,
$$\frac{6}{x+y}=\frac{1.5}{y}$$
Therefore,
$$6y=1.5(x+y)$$
$$6y=1.5x+1.5y$$
$$4.5y=1.5x$$
Hence,
$$y=\frac{x}{3}$$

(b)
Differentiating $y=\frac{x}{3}$ with respect to time,
$$\frac{dy}{dt}=\frac{1}{3}\frac{dx}{dt}$$
Given that $\frac{dx}{dt}=1.2\ \text{m/s}$,
$$\frac{dy}{dt}=\frac{1.2}{3}=0.4\ \text{m/s}$$
Thus, the shadow is increasing in length at $0.4\ \text{m/s}$.

(c)
Let $z=x+y$ be the distance of the tip of the shadow from the lamp post. Therefore,
$$\frac{dz}{dt}=\frac{dx}{dt}+\frac{dy}{dt}$$
$$\frac{dz}{dt}=1.2+0.4=1.6\ \text{m/s}$$
Hence, the tip of the shadow is moving away from the lamp post at $1.6\ \text{m/s}$.
